analysis: The PR changes two golden test fixtures under libs/darkbloom-cluster/Tests/PlacementChecks/Golden/layouts/ (gemma-4-26b-qat-4bit.json and gemma-4-26b.json). Each change is a single-line modification that adds a `routedExperts` object ({loadedBytes, routing:{experts:128, selected:8}}) to the layout JSON, with the value 12846366720 for the QAT 4-bit model and 24265359360 for the full model. No other field was visibly altered; the visible patch prefixes match, including artifactSHA256, configurationSHA256, requestChargeEveryRankBytes and the layers. The patch excerpts are truncated, so a full line diff was not performed, but the base and head text for the QAT file are fully supplied and appear identical apart from the added field. These are test data files, not runtime code. They hold no secrets, keys, credentials or attestation material, and they change no provider/coordinator wire contract, authorization, encryption or cache code. No threat-model asset or boundary (TB-002, TB-007, TB-011, T-041, etc.) is touched by these fixtures. I found no concrete security regression. Open questions for integration: the consuming placement code (not supplied) must parse `routedExperts` and account for the extra memory in admission/placement. If it ignores the field or the golden check is lenient, memory-budget admission could be under-counted, which is an availability or correctness concern. That cannot be verified from the supplied evidence, so I note it as an unverified contract rather than a finding. The cluster pipeline code that generates and verifies these layouts was not supplied.
